newsitem.title: USA: Kmart improved sales boost second-quarter profits.
newsitem.headline: Kmart improved sales boost second-quarter profits.

text.p: Kmart Corp., the nation's third-largest retailer, Thursday reported a 35 percent rise in second-quarter operating profits and surprisingly strong earnings, crediting higher sales in most merchandise categories.
Net income from continuing operations rose to $31 million, or 6 cents a share, from $23 million, or 5 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter, the Troy, Mich.-based company said.

Overall net income fell to $31 million, or 6 cents a share, from $34 million, or 5 cents a share, in the 1996 period because Kmart sold its struggling Builders Square home improvement chain to investment bank Leonard Green & Partners LP in July. Builders Square accounted for $11 million in profits a year ago.
But the profit topped Wall Street's consensus forecast for 4 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analyst estimates.
Kmart stock rose 31 cents to $12.06 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most actively traded shares on volume of 2.4 million.
Kmart rang up $7.85 billion in total sales, a 3.7 percent increase from $7.57 billion in 1996's second quarter. Comparable-store sales -- by stores open at least a year -- increased 5.5 percent.
"Sales in our U.S. Kmart stores increased 5.6 percent on a comparable store basis for the first six months of 1996, which meets our expectations," Chairman Floyd Hall said in a statement.
"Strong sales also helped expense ratios," he said.
Sales of housewares and home decor, cosmetics and fragrances, and consumables -- quick-turnover items such as soft drinks, snacks and socks -- showed strength, said Hall.

Kmart has been disappointed by sales of women's apparel this year, but the company is entering the third quarter with seasonal inventory levels below last year's and expects improvements in the second half, Hall said in a statement.
For the first half, Kmart's income from continuing operations was $45 million, or 9 cents a share, vs. a loss of $13 million, or 2 cents a share last year.
First-half net income was $45 million, or 9 cents a share, compared with a loss of $65 million, or 13 cents a share, in 1996. Sales rose to $15.1 billion from $14.5 billion.
Kmart, which operates 2,122 Kmart, Big Kmart and Super Kmart retail outlets, is the third-largest U.S. retailer after Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and Sears, Roebuck & Co.
